parsed.population_and_sample: Three nonstate leaders and their associates and communities involved in urban wastewater and fecal-sludge management: the Art of Living Foundation in Delhi, Dr. Veer Bhadra Mishra and the Sankat Mochan Foundation in Varanasi, and Safai Karmachari Andolan/manual scavengers nationally.
parsed.exposure: Institutional fragmentation, regulatory enforcement and legal exceptionalism, data-scarce sanitation planning, exclusion of nonstate evidence from administrative decisions, and nonenforcement of laws prohibiting manual scavenging.
parsed.outcome: Disconnected or unavailable sanitation services, untreated wastewater discharge, inadequate treatment capacity, unsafe fecal-sludge disposal, and continued reliance on excluded and endangered manual-scavenging workers.
parsed.rationale: The Introduction states that the authors examine wastewater and fecal-sludge-management gaps through the activities and perspectives of three nonstate leaders and their communities, and Section 2 presents these as three case studies. Sections 2.1–2.3 empirically describe how regulatory decisions, administrative conflict, deficient measurement, and failure to enforce labor law sustained untreated sewage, inadequate treatment capacity, and unsafe manual scavenging; the Conclusion synthesizes these sanitation-access and service-chain outcomes.
